title: Proofs of the Self
claim: Recognition is not a belief to be adopted but a conclusion to be earned: three treatises prove the subject is not inert, the agent is universal, and the relation between the two is real — in one terse reference volume.

purpose.impact: The rational case for recognition, compressed until the reader cannot dismiss it as mysticism.
purpose.reader: The philosopher, the sceptic, and the practitioner who needs a reason before a practice.
purpose.realisation: If the subject is not inert, the agent is universal, and the relation is real, then recognition is a conclusion — not a belief and not an experience.
non_goals: no expanded commentary in this volume

pages.note: 106 verses at 2–3/pp (36–53pp) + 9 essays + front 10 + glossary 8 + index 6 + end 4 = 73–90, padded to 108.

sections_plan.purpose: the perceiver cannot be inert matter
the subject is conscious and self-luminous
the subject is free agency, not an object

inclusion: all verses of the source, in order, set continuously at two to three per page

all 106 verses of the three siddhis, set continuously at two to three per page
nine chapter essays placed from ARGMAP + C1; glossary and index generated
exclusion: no verse may be selected away to make room — the argument requires the whole set
no verse from this source may appear in another book
no facing-page commentary in the reference edition; that is the expanded edition's job
no verse is selected away; the argument needs the whole set
this volume is the terse reference — the expanded critical edition is a later edition, not a second volume
